title: Who pays more?

predict.q: Same two markets as before. Now the students' demand grows: at every price, students want to buy more. What happens to the two prices?

options.fb: With constant MC the two markets are priced separately: the business market's MR = MC point has not moved, so its price stays 70.

options.s: The students' price falls: a bigger group gets a bigger discount.
options.fb: This is not a bulk discount. With more demand at every price, students' demand is less elastic at each price, so their MR = MC price rises.

options.s: The students' price rises; the business price stays at 70.
options.fb: The students' MR = MC point moves out: their price rises (30 → 35 → … → 70) and their PED falls in size towards −1.4. The business market is unchanged.

options.s: Neither price changes: costs are the same as before.
options.fb: Costs have not changed, but price also depends on demand: the students' MR curve has shifted, so their MR = MC price is higher.

task: Move the students' demand slider up and watch each price and each PED.

target.do: Move the students' demand slider up, then press Check.

takeaway: Each market has its own MR = MC price. The less elastic group pays more; when both groups have the same PED, they pay the same price.
